- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often overcorrects downward — adjust upward to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- Model frequently overestimates short-term spikes (e.g., +5–10% above recent high) — cap forecast at 1.1x recent peak unless sentiment confirms breakout.  
- After a sharp price rise, model often fails to capture mean reversion — reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days if sentiment turns neutral or slightly negative.  
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 3+ days, model tends to lag — forecast should be 1–2% ahead of true price to capture sentiment-driven momentum.  
- Model underestimates long-term trend (30d) when sentiment is bullish — add 2–5% buffer to forecast if sentiment > 0.67 for 5+ consecutive days.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out — use median of recent 3–5 day sentiment to adjust forecast direction.  
- If true outcome exceeds model by > 3% for 2+ consecutive days, model is underestimating — apply “lag correction” by +1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
